trials.notes: Used the correct `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` choice for body-fragment, structure-aware text extraction. Every called method is documented in the supplied markdown: `next_token`, `get_token_type`, `get_modifiable_text`, `get_tag`, `is_tag_closer`, and `get_attribute`. The one-pass token/state approach matches the documented closer-driven pattern, filters to ordinary `#text` tokens, requires `is_string( $href )`, and handled decoded attributes/text plus unclosed input. No `_doing_it_wrong` records.

Essentially matches the canonical documented pattern: create an HTML fragment processor, `next_tag( 'A' )`, require a string-valued `href`, then perform a depth-bounded `next_token()` subtree walk collecting only `#text` via `get_modifiable_text()`. All methods are documented and no misuse was recorded.

Used the correct HTML Processor and a documented single-cursor token-walk state machine. It used only documented methods, checked string-valued `href`, collected decoded ordinary text tokens, used depth to detect leaving the anchor subtree, and retained a final EOF flush for incomplete/unclosed input. No `_doing_it_wrong` records.

failure_analysis: All three trials passed all 8 frozen cases, so there were no failed hidden cases to attribute to documentation gaps. The docs did well on the core concepts this task needed: `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor` overview says it has no tree awareness and points structural text extraction to `WP_HTML_Processor`; `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` explains body-fragment construction; `WP_HTML_Processor::next_token()` documents subtree walking, virtual closers for unclosed elements, and depth-bounded scans; `get_attribute()`/Tag Processor docs document `string|true|null`, decoded attribute values, and boolean valueless attributes; `get_modifiable_text()` documents decoded `#text` values and warns not to use it as a text-node predicate. Near-miss: the `next_token()` warning about nested loops could be read as conflicting with the depth-bounded recipe used by trial-2/reference, but the examples were sufficient for these subjects.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor method entry documents `string|true|null` but does not repeat the Tag Processor's clearer wording that string attribute values are already decoded, `href=""` is a string, valueless attributes return `true`, and absent/unavailable attributes return `null`.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Mirror the decoded-value and empty-string/boolean/null examples directly in the HTML Processor inherited method docs so users do not have to cross-read the Tag Processor page.

doc_gaps.problem: The warning against nested `next_token()` loops is useful but broad; readers could over-apply it to the safe pattern of `next_tag()` followed by one depth-bounded `next_token()` subtree scan.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that the risky shape is an outer `next_token()` loop with an inner consuming walk, and state that `next_tag()` plus a depth-bounded subtree scan is valid when the next search should resume after the boundary token.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say virtual closers are visited for unclosed elements and separately mention `paused_at_incomplete_token()`, but there is no compact example showing what a read-only extractor can expect from an unclosed element or trailing incomplete syntax.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small generic example showing accumulated text from an unclosed element and explain when returning partial data is acceptable versus when callers should reject based on `paused_at_incomplete_token()` or `get_last_error()`.
